title: Nate Lowman: Before and After

description.main: The first comprehensive monograph on the American painter Nate Lowman (b. 1979), published by Aspen Art Press to accompany his survey at the Aspen Art Museum in 2017-18. 240 pages with 80 color and 20 black-and-white plates, and texts by Jim Lewis and Heidi Zuckerman.
description.extended:
The first comprehensive monograph on the American painter Nate Lowman (b. 1979), published by Aspen Art Press to accompany his survey at the Aspen Art Museum in 2017-18.

The Aspen exhibition, organized by Lowman with the museum's director Heidi Zuckerman, hung more than sixty paintings salon-style across two galleries, from canvases finished in 2003 to work completed weeks before the opening. Most were borrowed from private collections in the United States and Europe. The book reproduces roughly fifteen years of paintings, sculptures and installations in 80 color and 20 black-and-white plates, with texts by Jim Lewis and Zuckerman. Its white jacket carries only the title, the publisher and the ISBN, set in Helvetica.

Lowman builds his paintings out of images already in circulation: bullet holes, smiley faces, pine-tree air fresheners, poppies, crosses, tabloid photographs of Julia Roberts and Joan Rivers. He prints, crops, projects, stains, lacquers and restretches them until the source has been visibly worked over. He lives and works in New York and is represented by David Zwirner.
description.artist_bio: Nate Lowman (b. 1979, Las Vegas) is a painter and sculptor based in New York. He works with appropriated imagery drawn from American mass culture and news media, and is represented by David Zwirner.
description.exhibition_context: Nate Lowman: Before and After, Aspen Art Museum, Aspen, Colorado, December 15, 2017 - June 10, 2018. Organized by the artist with museum director Heidi Zuckerman; installed salon-style in Galleries 2 and 3.

notes: Published to accompany "Nate Lowman: Before and After," Aspen Art Museum, 15 December 2017 - 10 June 2018. Texts by Jim Lewis and Heidi Zuckerman.

research_log.conflicts_resolved: The David Zwirner product page lists 72 pages, staple bound, 84 color reproductions. ARTBOOK/D.A.P. and OpenLibrary both give 240 pages, hardcover, 80 color + 20 b&w. Went with 240pp hardcover on the two-source agreement.
